title: The body of Christ (CCC 787–796)
hookLine: the Church is one body with many members

cards: A road outside Damascus. A man named Saul is on his way to arrest followers of Jesus, letters of authority in his bag.
A light from heaven flashes around him, he falls to the ground, and a voice asks: "Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me?" Not why do you persecute my followers. Not my friends.
Me. Saul becomes Paul, and one picture he reaches for, to explain that voice, is your own body.

teach.h: THE BODY IS ONE, WITH MANY MEMBERS.
teach.b: Paul's picture, in the Douay-Rheims: "For as the body is one, and hath many members; and all the members of the body, whereas they are many, yet are one body, so also is Christ."
Then he says it straight: you are the body of Christ, and each of you a member. He imagines body parts arguing. The foot says, since I'm not a hand, I'm not part of the body.
The eye would like to tell the hand, I don't need your help. Neither, Paul says, can be true.
Then he flips the usual ranking: the parts that seem weaker are the ones that are necessary.
"And if one member suffer any thing, all the members suffer with it; or if one member glory, all the members rejoice with it." Stub your toe and your whole body winces.
That's what Paul says a church is meant to feel like. The Catechism teaches that Christ is the head of this body, and that the Spirit gives the members different gifts for the good of the whole.
Catholics say body of Christ at two moments that turn out to be connected. When the priest holds up the host at communion and says the body of Christ, the person receiving says amen.
Augustine told new Christians in his sermons that with that amen they're saying yes to what they themselves are: the body of Christ.
Be what you see, he said, and receive what you are.

teach.h: YOU ARE THE BODY OF CHRIST.
teach.b: So the stranger in the next pew, whose name you don't know, is part of the same body. That's what Saul heard on the road.

how: At communion the minister says the body of Christ and each person answers amen, and in the prayers of the faithful at Mass the parish prays together for its members, especially the sick and those who have died.

o: Jesus's body as it was laid in the tomb
the clergy, set apart from ordinary believers
the Church as one body, with Christ its head

games.q: what's inside the word — tap the pairs.
p: can't say I don't need you

s: the voice on the road asked Saul why he persecuted Jesus's followers
it asked: why persecutest thou me? Jesus identifies with his people.
in the Catholic Church, body of Christ can mean the Eucharist and the Church
Augustine connected the two: say amen to what you are.
Paul says the weaker parts of the body matter least
he flips the ranking: the parts that seem weaker are necessary.

games.q: you're Paul. a church is splitting into people who think they matter more and people who think they don't belong. what picture do you use?
games.why: one body with many members, where no part can say I don't need you, and all suffer and rejoice together.

practice: If you go to church, picture the people you see every week but have never met: the older man in the back, the family that's always late, the woman who sits alone; if you don't, choose a stranger from your street, your office, your bus.
Hold one of them in mind; you don't know their story, and they're part of the same body anyway. If you pray, you can pray for them.

wordCard.voice: Soma christou, Paul's Greek for the body of Christ: many members, one body, with Christ as its head. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: many members, one body. One member's sorrow or joy is everyone's news. Day three hundred eighteen, done.
